sections.heading: C - Distractions and driving challenges
sections.markdown:
## C - Distractions and driving challenges (Section 11)
Intro: Utah Section 11 covers distraction control and hazard response for tough settings [A01].

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
Anything drawing mind or body away from driving counts as a distraction and crash hazard [A01].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Utah road rage tied to a roadway criminal offense can bring a one-year license suspension on first conviction [A01].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A02
Adults need seven to nine hours of sleep to stay alert, so do not start a long trip tired [A02].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A03
When fatigue hits, leave the road at an exit or rest area for a twenty-minute power nap [A03].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A03
Six inches of water can stall most cars, while two feet of moving water can carry away most vehicles [A03].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A04
Drivers over eighteen may talk on a handheld device only with voice commands for hands-free calling [A04].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A80
A texting conviction carries a Class C misdemeanor and a fine capped at one hundred dollars. Causing bodily injury or having an earlier violation of this offense raises it to a Class B misdemeanor [A80].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A04
Work zone signs are orange with black letters, and speeding there draws at least twice the normal fine [A04].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A05
Dim high beams within five hundred feet of oncoming traffic and within three hundred feet when following [A05].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A06
Use lights whenever you cannot see one thousand feet ahead, and look to the right if blinded [A06].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A06
Cars can hydroplane above thirty-five miles per hour, and black ice looks like a wet spot [A06].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A07
If the rear slides right steer right, if it slides left steer left, ease off gas and avoid hard braking [A07].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A07
A car entering water floats only thirty to sixty seconds, so remove the belt and open a window fast [A07].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A08
Studded snow tires may be used from October fifteenth through March thirty-first each year [A08].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A09
If stranded in cold, run the engine about ten minutes each hour and keep one window cracked [A09].
Why it matters: high test value.
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0074]

Misconceptions: swerving for animals is safer, high beams help in fog, coasting saves fuel [A02].
Mnemonic: DEAL Devices off, Eat early, Animals alert, Leave space [A01].
Glossary: fatigue is tired mind-body slowing reactions, hydroplaning is tires on water [A06].
High-yield rank: night distances, flood depths, skid recovery, handheld rules, work fines [A04].
Dynamic isolation: no officeholder or fee facts here, desert heat notes stay as stable guidance [A02].
